Open-source AI just overtook the closed frontier.

Moonshot AI dropped Kimi K3 this week — 2.8 trillion parameters, the largest open-source model ever released. On coding benchmarks, it outperformed leading closed US systems. And by late July, anyone can download and adapt it for free.

This changes the math for every enterprise running AI. When open-source models match proprietary performance on tasks like code generation, the advantages of ownership become enormous. You control fine-tuning. You control deployment. You control your inference costs. No API lock-in. No per-token tax at scale.

Cognition already proved the downstream velocity — shipping SWE-1.7 as a fine-tune of the Kimi architecture at 1,000 tokens per second. Open foundations do not just match closed models. They accelerate entire ecosystems around them.

The new competitive divide is not access to frontier AI. It is the engineering capability to deploy and customize it. Organizations with strong AI teams just gained a structural edge.
